findings.title: Differently cased symlink excludes still fail to protect mirror destinations
findings.evidence: crates/blit-core/src/transfers/filter.rs:444 — stored_name returns None for every symlink at line 450, so stored_spelling preserves its typed case. Reproduced on case-insensitive macOS with src/cache pointing to an outside directory: excluding absolute src/CACHE produced ./CACHE in both the local filter and wire spec, without a warning. Mirroring into a destination containing cache/saved.txt deleted that file and its directory. Repeating with absolute src/cache preserved them.
findings.predicted_failure: A mirror can delete pre-existing destination data inside a directory explicitly excluded through a differently cased source symlink. This leaves cr-g3fix-1 materially open; the observed consequence is data loss.
findings.better_approach: Recover the symlink entry's own stored spelling without following its target, and preserve that spelling in both filter representations. Add a case-insensitive regression that verifies an existing destination subtree survives.

findings.title: Canonicalized literal prefixes are reinterpreted as glob syntax
findings.evidence: crates/blit-core/src/transfers/filter.rs:309 — resolved.join(rest) inserts canonical filesystem names into the pattern without escaping their glob metacharacters. Reproduced with alias pointing to src/data[1] and exclude alias/*.txt: both builders emitted data[1]/*.txt. The CLI copied data[1]/private.txt but omitted the unrelated data1/private.txt, exiting successfully without an unmatchable warning.
findings.predicted_failure: An alias resolving into a directory whose name contains glob syntax excludes the wrong files while transferring the intended excluded files. An unmatched '[' in the resolved name can instead make a previously valid pattern fail validation.
findings.better_approach: Keep canonicalized literal components distinct from the user-written glob suffix, escape those literal components for the matcher, and append the suffix unchanged. Test aliases into directories containing brackets and Unix backslashes.
